title: Cost pressure and platform convenience sustain counterfeit purchasing while harm reporting and perceived seriousness remain low
source_unit: UK Intellectual Property Office, Counterfeit goods research (Wave 5), 2026 publication
geography: United Kingdom adults aged 18+; nationally representative survey with qualitative and communications-testing stages

denominator.unit: UK adults aged 18+ in the nationally representative Stage 1 online survey

ever_purchased.unit: percent who had ever made a counterfeit purchase

unintentional_purchase.unit: percent who had accidentally bought a counterfeit at some point

young_adult_exposure.unit: percent of 18–24 year-olds reporting an ever-purchase in 2025

observations.method: Wave 5 of a longitudinal counterfeit-purchasing tracker using a 15-minute online survey with quotas and ONS-linked weighting; core measures were compared with prior waves.
observations.uncertainty: The study measures self-reported purchasing and does not independently authenticate products, estimate total market value, or establish that cost-of-living pressure caused purchasing; some category definitions changed.
observations.subgroup: UK adults, especially younger and price-sensitive consumers, with comparisons by age, gender, social grade, region, and product category.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable current purchasing alongside rising ever-purchase among younger adults may reflect exposure, recall, category shifts, or improved recognition rather than a uniform expansion of demand.

denominator.unit: UK counterfeit-purchasing categories and respondents described in the tracker

marketplace_shift.value: Major online marketplaces and social media increasingly supply counterfeit goods, while smaller online retailers and some in-person routes declined

social_media_route.value: Social media and short-form video environments increasingly shape exposure and purchasing routes

unintentional_young_adult_purchase.value: Unintentional purchase rose sharply among 18–24 year-olds, with over 30% indicating an unintentional purchase

verification.value: Weak product checks and platform-mediated discovery leave consumers exposed to deception

observations.method: Wave-on-wave tracker analysis supplemented by qualitative research on category-specific purchase routes and product checking.
observations.uncertainty: Channel shares vary by category and are not a causal estimate of platform effects; the report does not observe recommendation algorithms, seller enforcement, or individual transaction records.
observations.subgroup: Younger online shoppers, category-specific consumers, marketplace and social-media users, and consumers with different verification practices.
observations.counterinterpretation: Large marketplaces may be selected because they offer search, price comparison, reviews, and recourse cues, even when counterfeit detection remains imperfect.

denominator.unit: respondents who knowingly purchased counterfeit products in the previous 12 months and reported relevant experiences

negative_consequence.value: More than two-thirds reported at least one negative consequence

harm_types.value: Product failure, scams and financial loss, data-security risks, and health or safety risks in safety-critical categories

action_taken.unit: approximately percent of those with negative experiences who took action

recovery_condition.value: Most affected consumers did not report unless financial recovery was possible

observations.method: New Wave 5 harms module asking recent counterfeit purchasers about negative experiences and action, alongside reporting-channel questions.
observations.uncertainty: The harm module is new and has no historical trend baseline; experiences may have occurred at different times from the reported purchase, and conditional denominators should not be read as population prevalence.
observations.subgroup: Counterfeit purchasers, especially men, 18–24 year-olds, lower-income consumers, and respondents in London and the North West who showed higher reported exposure to negative outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Low reporting may reflect low perceived remedy value, uncertainty about jurisdiction, stigma, or transaction ambiguity rather than acceptance of harm alone.

observations.period: 2025; consumer language, moral distance, and segments

denominator.unit: UK counterfeit-purchaser segments and qualitative respondents

language.value: Younger purchasers often used softer terms such as fake, dupe, or lookalike

seriousness.value: Softer language corresponded with lower perceived seriousness and moral distance from illegality

moderate_segment.value: Trend-Responsive Bargain Seekers were described as 25–44, active online shoppers focused on fashion, sports, and technology; 31% distrusted warnings about potential harms

heavy_segment.value: Rebellious Value Activists were described as under 35, mainly male, buying across multiple categories; over half dismissed harm-related messaging

observations.method: IPO segmentation using self-declared purchasing behavior and number of categories, supplemented by qualitative interpretation and communications testing.
observations.uncertainty: Segments are analytic profiles rather than fixed social identities; language does not prove moral motivation, and communications-test responses do not establish behavior change.
observations.subgroup: Light, moderate, and heavy purchasers, with age, gender, online-shopping, category, and attitude differences.
observations.counterinterpretation: The language of dupes may describe perceived value and product similarity rather than deliberate denial of legal or safety consequences.

Full HTML report with methodology, category findings, harms, segmentation, and communications testing.

boundary: This record adds a consumer-recourse and platform-mediated authenticity layer. It is based primarily on self-reported UK consumer survey and qualitative evidence; it does not estimate the counterfeit market, authenticate individual goods, establish platform liability, identify causal effects of prices or social media, or measure completed enforcement or redress.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Full IPO Wave 5 HTML report reviewed for sample design, prevalence, price motivation, access routes, harms, reporting, segmentation, and methodological changes.
